instruction: `summarize(lines, min_level='INFO')` in logs.py is one monolithic loop that parses, filters and aggregates log lines. Refactor it into three composable module-level functions and make `summarize` a composition of them: (1) `parse_line(line) -> dict | None` returns {'level': str, 'component': str, 'message': str} for a well-formed line and None for a malformed one (same parsing rules as today); (2) `filter_level(records, min_level)` must be a LAZY generator (it must work on an infinite iterator) yielding records whose level is at or above min_level; (3) `count_by_component(records) -> dict[str, int]` counts records per component with keys in first-seen order. `summarize` must keep exactly its current return value and must not itself contain a for/while loop. Unknown `min_level` raises ValueError from both `filter_level` and `summarize`. All tests in tests/test_logs.py must pass.
